device_authorization.scope: Documentation supplement only; it is not an OpenAPI operation and is not included in operation_count_observed.
facts: The guide describes device authorization for interactive clients: a device_code and user_code, browser approval, and a token poll with grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code. Earlier revisions named RFC 8628 explicitly; upstream commit 2f2bdf3148 (2026-09-26, "docs: rebuild guides around current Kaneo workflows") dropped the name but not the grant.
It documents POST /api/auth/device/code, browser approval, then POST /api/auth/device/token; the issued token is sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

It states that self-hosted Kaneo allows the built-in device client IDs kaneo-cli and kaneo-mcp by default, and other IDs require DEVICE_AUTH_CLIENT_IDS approval. Its examples use the kaneo-cli client ID so they work with the default allowlist.
It tells clients to respect the returned polling interval, increase it on slow_down, stop when the code expires or access is denied, and never log device codes or access tokens.
gaps: The vendored OpenAPI snapshot contains GET /auth/device but does not contain the documented POST /auth/device/code or POST /auth/device/token endpoints, so neither is mapped as an OpenAPI operation.

The authentication guide gives examples, polling error names and polling rules but does not establish this CLI's storage policy, browser-launch behavior, or complete machine-readable request and response schemas. The client ID gap closed: the guide now uses kaneo-cli in its examples, the CLI's default.

The guide says most application requests need an Authorization: Bearer credential without listing the exceptions; individual OpenAPI operations can override inherited security, so implementation follows the endpoint-level OpenAPI security declaration and verifies live behavior. Earlier revisions said all API endpoints require authentication.

organization_role.scope: CLI query supplement only. The pinned OpenAPI and generated source inventory remain unchanged.
organization_role.evidence: Disposable pinned Kaneo v2.25.0: roleId and roleName each returned HTTP 200 and the newly created organization role when organizationId was supplied. See docs/verification.md.
organization_role.constraints: Exactly one non-empty roleId or roleName; optional non-empty organizationId, otherwise the server uses the active organization.

task_reserved_statuses.relationship: The pinned OpenAPI still describes task status as an unconstrained string and PUT /task/status/{id} as a move to another column. At v2.46.2 the declaring file still defines VIRTUAL_STATUSES as ["planned", "archived"], includes them in valid task statuses, and maps unknown import statuses to planned with a warning. This supplement is help text only; it is evidence for the contract, not a modification of the pinned snapshot.
task_reserved_statuses.scope: CLI help supplement only. The pinned OpenAPI, the generated operation inventory and the generated request-body reference remain unchanged.
task_reserved_statuses.evidence: Disposable pinned Kaneo (image digest recorded in docs/verification.md): writing status "planned" or "archived" through updateTaskStatus returned HTTP 200 with columnId null and moved the task into the board's plannedTasks or archivedTasks container; writing a column slug back restored it with a non-null columnId. createTask accepted "planned" directly. moveTask rejected destinationStatus "planned" with HTTP 400 "Selected status is not valid for the destination project". An unknown status on updateTaskStatus returned HTTP 400 and left the task unchanged. importTasks accepted an unknown status, stored it as "planned" and reported success with a per-task warning. listTasks --status planned returned only the planned container. See docs/verification.md.
task_reserved_statuses.constraints: Valid task statuses are the project's column slugs plus the reserved values "planned" and "archived" (upstream VIRTUAL_STATUSES). A column may not be created with either reserved slug, so the board's three containers cannot collide. moveTask accepts destination column slugs only.

api_key_rate_limits.scope: Documented discrepancy; exact upstream snapshots remain unchanged.
api_key_rate_limits.relationship: The OpenAPI ApiKeyRateLimited description says X-RateLimit headers are only sent when the rate limit was hit, whereas the authentication guide describes them on successful API-key requests. Source apiKeyCheckHeaders returns window metadata for valid keys as well as window-limit denials, but quota-only denials have no X-RateLimit headers. Retry-After can be omitted when quota never refills. Non-key authentication limits have their own Retry-After behavior.
api_key_rate_limits.constraints: The CLI preserves stable rate_limited error classification without automatic retries or inventing a retry delay. startImportRun HTTP 429 may instead mean the server has reached its concurrent import limit; HTTP 409 indicates an active workspace import.
